messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] reserved-pool node preempt detected — pool=rsvd-pool-238 (az-west-1) tenant=pacifica-med. Affected nodes: 1/4. Symptoms: abrupt node eviction, pods in CrashLoopBackOff while trying to migrate. Pager: @mike_oncall

mike_oncall: Ack. Jumping on it. Can someone pull the node logs?

sara_ops: I'm seeing the node marked NotReady in k8s and then the cloud reported a preemption event. Node name: rsvd-238-node-2. Kernel logs show GPU ECC errors spiking.

julia_se: Customer impact? Pacifica-med is on dedicated reserved pool — are any of their long-running inference jobs hitting errors or dropped requests?

kevin_support: Support has one chat open with pacifica-med; they've reported increased latency and a couple timed-out inference calls in the last 6 minutes. Not yet a full outage. They're flagged P1 for Dedicated SLA. I've told them we're investigating and will follow up with ETA.

ryan_hw: From the hardware side, remote telemetry shows repeated ECC and PCIe link errors on GPU0 of rsvd-238-node-2. Recommend marking for replacement; possible GPU firmware/kernel panic.

mike_oncall: OK. Steps I'm taking now: 1) cordon & drain node, 2) failover tenant routes to warm instances, 3) create replacement VM in same pool. Running drain now: 

```
# kubectl cordon rsvd-238-node-2
node/rsvd-238-node-2 cordoned

# kubectl drain rsvd-238-node-2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force\warning: ignoring daemonsets in drain: kube-system/aws-node\pod/pm-infer-01 evicted\pod/pm-infer-02 evicted\pod/monitoring-agent evicted
node/rsvd-238-node-2 drained
```

mike_oncall: Drain completed, pods rescheduled to rsvd-238-node-4 and warm-pool instances. Not seeing CrashLoopBackOff now, but a couple of pods restarted during reschedule.

deploy-bot: Automation started: creating replacement instance for rsvd-238-node-2 (job id: repl-1845-07). Estimated provisioning time ~ 40-50m.

sara_ops: Routing update pushed: tenant pacifica-med traffic shifted to reserved-pool-237 and warm-pool-1. Monitoring alert thresholds temporarily relaxed for inflight calibrations.

julia_se: Noted. I'll coordinate with the customer TPM and offer a short post-call after replacement. Please capture info about failed inferences (request ids) so we can surface to them.

kevin_support: Got the request ids; logging them. Also recording customer-facing message to send after resolution.

ryan_hw: I've filed a hardware replacement and asked cloud provider to preserve the instance logs for warranty. Root cause preliminary: persistent ECC errors causing GPU driver to trigger nodal eviction. Will wait for the replacement hardware to validate.

mike_oncall: Handing off monitoring and followup to sara_ops for the remainder of the window. I'll stay reachable by DM for escalation. Current status: replacement VM provisioning, traffic on alternate nodes, customer aware.

sara_ops: Taking over. I'll update every 15m or on any regression. Setting a short-lived incident channel pin and adding replication of logs to /incident-archives/rsvd-238.

incident-bot: [INFO] replacement instance repl-1845-07 entered provisioning state. ETA 45m.

sara_ops: Quick note — we observed one inference job that retried 3x and returned inconsistent latencies (~1.2s -> 9s -> timeout). That job id: pm-job-9982. Filing as part of the incident packet.

deploy-bot: replacement instance repl-1845-07 is READY and joined cluster as rsvd-238-node-2-repl. Applying tags and node-labels.

mike_oncall: Nice. Bringing node into rotation: 

```
# kubectl uncordon rsvd-238-node-2-repl
node/rsvd-238-node-2-repl uncordoned
# kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep rsvd-238
 rsvd-238-node-2-repl Ready  
```

sara_ops: Rescheduled pacifica-med workloads back to the replaced node gradually (canary 1/4 -> 2/4 -> all). No regressions observed so far. Latency back to baseline for previously affected request ids.

julia_se: I'll schedule the customer follow-up in 1 hour to summarize actions and next steps.

ryan_hw: After replacement, collected GPU firmware + driver logs. Opening HW follow-up ticket with provider and vendor. Action items: schedule GPU firmware update on next maintenance window and add ECC monitoring alert at lower thresholds.

kevin_support: Customer notified of resolution. They'll wait for the formal postmortem.

mike_oncall: Closing active page from my side. Handed off monitoring to sara_ops per earlier. Final summary: preemption/eviction triggered by repeating ECC/PCIe link errors -> node drained and replaced -> traffic routed to alternates during replacement -> customer impact limited to elevated latency on a subset of requests.

sara_ops: Adding incident action items to the ticket: [1] Increase warm-pool reserve for enterprise reserved pools by +1, [2] Lower ECC alert threshold, [3] Run targeted firmware verification for rsvd-pool hardware. I'll open the postmortem doc and tag eng-runtime and eng-infra.

incident-bot: [CLOSED] Paging incident resolved and handed off to postmortem.
